findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a container of onion crunch topping to be stored with no protective covering. The container had package labeling sitting inside of the container contacting the food. The PIC was informed and the item was discarded. Ensure containers remain covered to prevent items from accidentally contaminating food surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a sanitizing cloth stored directly on the food contact surface of the sushi prep table. The PIC was informed and the cloth was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wet cloths are stored in sanitizing solution to prevent microbial growth.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the condensation catch canister of the rice cooker to be soiled with a pink residue. The PIC was informed and the item was moved to the dish area. Inspector also observed the gaskets of the coolers under the rice cooker to be heavily soiled. Ensure all parts of the rice cooker and coolers are washed and sanitized frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed on two different occasions rinsing hands in the hand-sink without following proper handwashing procedures. The activity was ceased and a discussion was had on proper handwashing procedures to correct the violation. When washing hands, be sure to rinse hands first, then add soap and lather hands for at least 10-15 seconds, rinse hands again, dry hands with a disposable towel, and then use towel to turn off faucet handles. Ensure that proper cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Observed several TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods stored in a prep cooler (and standing cooler) without proper dating marking. These items include crab meat, crushed tuna, cream cheese, shrimp, spicy mayonnaise, etc. PIC mentioned that items were prepared yesterday and will be discarded today. Discussed with PIC that these TCS foods must be date marked if held in house over night. 
Day 1 counts as the day that the items are made. There are 6 additional days that the items can be held in house before it must be discarded. At the end of day 7, the items must be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The PIC was beginning to food prep without having a sanitizer bucket available. The activity was ceased and the PIC was asked to create a sanitizer bucket. After preparing the bucket, the solution was tested at 200ppm(quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed handling a cell phone and then donning gloves without washing hands. Discussed proper handwashing techniques when switching tasks in between food handling. When handling cell phones, be sure to wash hands before putting on gloves to avoid contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed a container of sushi rice to be left on the counter overnight at room temperature for at least 12 hours. The facility acidifies white rice by adding vinegar to control bacteria growth. PIC mentioned that the rice can be held on the counter for 48 hours. According to the HACCP plan for the sushi rice, rice must be discarded if held longer than 10 hours. PIC also mentions that he mixes leftover rice with freshly made rice for the next morning. Never mix leftover rice with freshly cooked rice. Discussed proper holding for sushi rice. Sushi rice can only be kept up to 10 hours at a time and should be discarded if time exceeds. The leftover sushi rice was discarded by the PIC.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: The in house spicy mayonnaise stored in the prep cooler was observed without date marking at the start of the inspection. PIC provided date marking during the inspection with today’s date (4/30/2025). The mayo appeared to be prepared days prior. Discussed with PIC proper date marking. Spicy mayonnaise can only be held in house for no longer than 7 days. Day 1 counts as the day that the mayonnaise is made. There are 6 additional days that the sauce can be held in house before it shall be discarded. At the end of day 7, the sauce must be discarded. The correct date marking was added to the mayonnaise to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the facility to have some cooked boba, and three small quantities of tea mix unmarked in the reach-in cooler.  The items were discarded at the time of inspection. The facility stated that they are not using these items. The facility also stated that they had been in the cooler for a week. (Last Tuesday) Take care to removed items that are no longer in use, over seven days for date marking. This is a repeat violation and was corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a cardboard box used to store the pH meter and other testing items. Remove cardboard and replace with a smooth cleanable container. Also, cardboard is being used to line the bottom shelf of the reach in cooler. Remove cardboard and clean as necessary. 

4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Inspector observed employee drink to be sitting on the cart next to single use gloves, a knife and chili oil. The drink was discarded before the inspector could mention it. Store personal drinks in the paperwork area. Provide a lid and a straw to the cup, and wash hands properly after taking a break for a drink. 

2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Inspector observed Imitation crab meat to be tawing in the hand sink next to the three part sink. The food was moved to the reach in cooler. The violation is considered corrected on site. There are no prep sinks in the deli area. Food will have to be either thawed in the reach in cooler or in a bay of the 3 part sink that has been washed, rinsed and sanitized before use.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a container of brown sugar crystal boba on the counter at room temperature. (Approximately 4 lbs) The package states keep refrigerated after opening. Employee stated that he was trained that the product could be kept on the counter. The Product was discarded. The violation is considered to be corrected on site. Inspector looked at the HACCP plan and ACE documents in an attempt to verify whether or not the food could be stored at room temperature. Follow label directions for handling the food or provide a letter from Bossen that states their labeling is for quality and not for food safety.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed three tubs of tea mix and a storage container of boba with discard dates of 2/4/24. The tea was in the reach in cooler. The Boba beads were on the counter at room temperature. The items were discarded in the garbage. The violation is considered corrected on site. Follow date marking rules by discarding at proper intervals.
